gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Redux spaces its letters wide and swoops into every curve with a big, visible entrance. Noto Sans Kannada follows in a friendly sans-serif, with a gentle step up to capitals and wide-open s curves.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Redux stretches its letters out wide, with soft shifts in thickness that never turn stark and a generous lowercase. Noto Sans Kayah Li sits under it quietly.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, its curves never quite closing. Redux above it is lighter, with thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Noto Sans Khojki is a plain sans with a clear, large eye on every e and exits wide enough to pass light. Redux, with its modest curve stress, keeps it moving.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Noto Sans Khudawadi reads low and level, with capitals barely above the lowercase and rounds left open like an unlatched hook. Redux adds mild, visible contrast on top, which is the pair's real draw.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-kr: Redux leads with thick strokes that pull the eye along without taking over the line. Noto Sans KR then supplies the strongest quality, a big x-height with stubby ascenders and generous gaps in its curves.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-lao: Redux draws subtle but visible stroke modulation, spaced wide. Its job is to show off those curves and entrances, while Noto Sans Lao, a sans-serif with a tall x-height and open mouths on c, e and a, simply carries the text.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped reads in solid blocks rather than skylines, its bowls left unfinished on one side. And Redux above it changes weight in ways that are present but never dramatic.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable is the first word for Redux, with its wide spacing and gently modulated stroke weight. Noto Sans Lepcha follows with lowercase carrying the stature of cast iron capitals and curves that keep a wide opening.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Contemporary lines run through Redux, which spaces its geometric letters wide and has stems just a touch thicker than the connecting strokes. And Noto Sans Limbu, a plain sans with tall-bodied small letters and gaping curves, meets it with an open face.
